texts.preamble: Anil Kumar Azad ... vs Shyam Lal Tyagi on 3 April, 2025 In The Court Of Dr. Ruchi Aggarwal Asrani Presiding Officer, Mact-01 (Central) Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Dlct010052092018 Mact No. : 324/2018 Fir No. : 113/2018 Ps : Kashmere Gate
texts.facts: The accident took place with the vehicle i.e. UP Roadways Bus bearing registration No. UP-30AT-2529, driven rashly and negligently by respondent no. 1, Shyam Lal Tyagi and owned by respondent no.2, UP Roadways. The vehicle is stated to be not insured. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that information of an accident was received at P.S. Kashmere Gate vide DD No. 24 PP on 29.09.2017. ASI Rakesh Kumar went to the spot where the injured Anil Kumar Azad was found lying, the bus of UP Roadways bearing registration no. UP-30-AT-2529 was stationed at Platform No. 7 and its driver, Shyam Lal Tyagi, was also present there. The injured was sent to Trauma Centre in PCR van. In the meantime, Ct. Jai Prakash also came there. After leaving him at the spot, ASI Rakesh Kumar went to Trauma Centre, Civil Lines and collected MLC No.13279/17 of the injured. Although, the petitioner was stated to be fit for statement but he did not make any statement on that day. The offending bus as well as its driver were kept under observation at the police station. On 30.09.2017, ASI Rakesh Kumar again went to Trauma Centre along with the driver of the offending bus but the injured did not make any statement on that day also and therefore, the driver and the offending bus were released subject to certain terms and conditions. Thereafter, ASI Rakesh again contacted the injured but he informed that he is undergoing private treatment and due to the said accident, his left leg has been damaged. ASI Rakesh went to the residence of the injured at Kota, Rajasthan and recorded his statement wherein he stated that on 29.09.2017, he reached at ISBT, Kashmere Gate to go to Meerut, UP and at about 08:30 P.M., he was waiting for the bus and there was very heavy rush due to Dussehra festival. In the meantime, bus of UP Roadways was about to park at platform No.7 and the passengers waiting for the said bus rushed towards the said bus and he was also going towards the said bus from platform no. 5 to platform no. 7 but in the meantime, his left leg got stuck between the divider and rear wheel of the said bus and his leg got dragged by the bus for a distance. The people from crowd shouted but by then, he had suffered grievous injury in his leg. He further stated in his statement that some unknown person from the crowd called at 100 number and the police had come at the spot of the accident. He also stated that due to the said accident, his left leg has been amputated and he has become handicapped and therefore, appropriate legal action be taken against the driver of the offending vehicle who was driving the bus in very rash and negligent manner. After coming back to Delhi, he submitted the MLC of the injured for final opinion as per which, the injury suffered by the petitioner was grievous. On the basis of the statement of the petitioner and his MLC, the offence under Section 279/338 of IPC was found to have been committed and accordingly, FIR No. 113/2018 was registered at P.S. Kashmere Gate and investigation of the matter was assigned to ASI Bal Hussain. 3. During the course of investigation, on 24.032018, ASI Bal Husain had prepared the site plan at the instance of ASI Rakesh Kumar. In the meantime, Sh. Shyam Lal Tyagi, the driver of the offending bus also came there along with the offending bus and ASI Rakesh identified him to be the same driver who caused the accident in question. The IO arrested the driver, however, since the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds. On 27.03.2018, the driving license of the driver and documents of the offending vehicle were seized by the IO. Mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle was got conducted. The documents pertaining to the offending vehicle were got verified from the concerned authority and found to be valid. On completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle before the court of the concerned Ld. JMFC and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 17.04.2018. 4. Separate written statements were filed on behalf of respondent nos.1 & 2 wherein, they have denied all the allegations made in the DAR. Respondent no.1 stated in his written statement that on 29.09.2017, he was trying to park the bus on the platform no.7 at ISBT, Kashmiri Gate Bus Terminal, Delhi to board the passengers in the bus in a very dead slow speed. He also stated that there was a lot of rush at the ISBT due to Dussehra festival and the petitioner/injured was in so much hurry and he was trying to board/enter in the bus from the driver side window and due to this reason, injured/petitioner fell down and received injuries due to his own negligence. He further stated that the DAR has been filed after almost six months after the incident with the convenience of the injured/petitioner. Respondent no. 2 has also stated the same facts in his written statement. 5. The petitioner has also filed his replication to the written statement filed by respondent no.1. ISSUES FRAMED 6. On the basis of the pleading of the parties, vide order dated 26.02.2019, this Tribunal had framed the following issues: 1. OPP. 3. Relief. EVIDENCE 7. To prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1, Mr. Pushkar Raj Meena as PW-2, Mr. Satyajeet Kumar as PW-3, Mr. Anil Kumar as PW-4 and Dr. Rajesh Goel, Professor and Head of the Department of Orthopedics, Medical College, Kota, Rajasthan as PW-5. The petitioner closed his evidence on 30.11.2024. The respondent no. 1 did not lead any evidence. Respondent no. 2 examined Sh. Amit Kumar Saini as R2W-1. Respondents' evidence was closed vide order dated 25.01.2025. 8. The Petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner has been recorded. The petitioner (PW-1) testified that due to the accident, he sustained grievous injuries and his left leg was amputated. 18. Furthermore, the petitioner was examined by the Medical Board at M. B. S. Hospital, Kota and vide certificate bearing No. 13 dated 03.05.2018, it has been observed that the petitioner has suffered "Above knee amputation of left lower leg resulting in 80% (Eighty) permanent physical disability in relation to whole body corresponding to injury reports treatment record. 19. The petitioner also examined Dr. Rajesh Goel who was a member of the Medical Board that examined the disability of the injured. He was examined as PW-5 and deposed as under: "...I state that I was one of the members of the Disability Assessment Board constituted by the Medical Superintendent of Medical College, Kota, Rajasthan, whereby we had examined Sh. Anil Kumar Azad for disability. The petitioner/injured has claimed Rs. 8,12,805/- under this head. The petitioner examined Mr. Satyajit Kumar, Prosthetist & Orthotist, Endolite Prosthetic & Orthotic Centre, Naraina, Delhi as PW-3 who proved the Quotation for Endolite Transfemoral Prsothesis (Artificial Limb) as Ex. PW-3/2 (colly.) In his cross-examination, he stated that "The starting price of prosthesis is Rs. 3.5 Lakhs approximately but the most suitable for the injured in the present case is for Rs. 8 lakhs for which I have brought the quotation Ex. PW-3/2. Therefore, the petitioner/ injured is awarded a compensation of Rs. 8,12,805/- under this head.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. 11. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner argued that the accident occurred due to the sole Anil Kumar Azad ... vs Shyam Lal Tyagi on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65877496/ 6 negligence of respondent no. 1. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 argued that the petitioner was himself negligent and responsible for the accident as he was in a lot of rush to get into the bus. He further submitted that because the petitioner was trying to get into the bus from the side of the driver, his leg got crushed between the bus and footpath without any fault of the driver of the bus. He submitted that the conductor of the bus, Mr. Amit Kumar Saini, as R2W1 wherein he deposed as under: "...4. That on 29.09.2017, the driver of the alleged bus was trying to stand/park the bus on the platform No. 7 at ISBT, Kashmiri Gate Bus Terminal, Delhi, to board the passenger in the bus in a very dead slow speed. The ISBT was packed as a heavy rush due to the Dusshera festival, a passenger/ petitioner was in a very much hurry and he was trying to board/ enter in the bus from the driver side window and due to this reason, the petitioner fell down and he received injuries. There was fault on the part of the petitioner himself, who in hurry could not take care of himself and his leg slipped from the path." 14. While in his examination in chief, R2W1 has deposed that the petitioner was trying to board the bus through the window on the side of the driver but in his cross-examination, he has categorically admitted that he had "not seen the injured trying to board our bus through the window on the driver's side". He has also admitted that "It is correct that I have not seen the injured trying to get inside the bus with my own eye." 15. Further, the respondent no.1, who was the driver of the vehicle, would have been the most crucial witness capable of refuting the petitioner's allegations of the occurrence of the accident and rash and negligent driving. and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no.1, Shyam Lal Tyagi (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases Anil Kumar Azad ... vs Shyam Lal Tyagi on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65877496/ 8 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). 9. But if the Anil Kumar Azad ... vs Shyam Lal Tyagi on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65877496/ 11 Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent. The determination of damages on account of pain and suffering, loss of amenities and loss of expectation of life would depend upon the age of Anil Kumar Azad ... vs Shyam Lal Tyagi on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65877496/ 12 victim, nature of injury(ies)/deprivation/disability suffered by victim and the effect thereof on life of the petitioner. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim. Accordingly, the Multiplier of nine (09) is taken for purposes of calculating the loss of income of the petitioner (Reliance is placed on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Pranay Sethi & Ors., Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, date of decision - 31.10.2017). Further, by adopting the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC), the future prospects of Anil Kumar Azad shall be 10% as he was within the age bracket of 50-60 years at the time of accident on 29.09.2017. 34. In the case of Benson George v Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. in Civil Appeal No. 1540 of 2022 decided on 25.02.2022, Hon'ble Supreme Court had awarded an interest of 6% per annum.
